prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Image1 costume and painted material identity reference; Image2 is an EXACT TWELVE-FRAME POSE GUIDE, 4 columns x 3 rows. Draw a finished realistic soldier walk-cycle atlas using Image2's limb poses in each corresponding cell. This is a targeted corrective redraw of the walking poses: the legs in Image1 repeat the same foot-forward pose incorrectly. Follow Image2's leg positions much more strictly than Image1. Image2 red means NEAR leg, blue means FAR leg; these colors are guides ONLY and must NOT appear in finished art. Both legs should be ordinary matching dark gray trousers/black leather boots, near leg slightly lighter, far leg slightly darker.
Preserve Image1 adult male identity: grey-green heavy long weathered greatcoat, olive steel helmet, round glass gas mask and filter, brown straps, small chest pouches, detailed realistic painted cloth and leather. Side camera faces RIGHT for all twelve drawings, same camera/scale/lighting/torso/proportions. True transparent alpha background, no background, text, grid, floor, guide lines, anatomy markers or colors. Omit BOTH arms entirely below shoulder sockets, gun, slung rifle, satchel, bedroll, canteen: those are runtime parts. Keep torso chest pouches and harness.
Precisely FOUR columns THREE rows, chronological ONE complete gait cycle, one isolated full-body drawing per equal cell, fully visible helmet and feet, generous gutters. Pose1 near foot forward contact and far foot back; pose2 near supports and far pushes off; pose3 near boot under pelvis and far heel lifted behind; pose4 near support leg under pelvis and FAR boot passing forward OFF THE FLOOR; pose5 near boot behind pelvis, FAR knee and boot swinging forward; pose6 near foot back, FAR foot descending in front. Pose7 the opposite contact: FAR leg is forward, NEAR leg is BACK; pose8 near foot lifted behind, far supports; pose9 near heel higher behind with flexed knee, far foot under pelvis; pose10 FAR supporting straight leg under pelvis, NEAR knee lifted and NEAR BOOT CLEARLY OFF GROUND passing forward (MUST visibly differ from pose4); pose11 NEAR knee swings forward above far foot; pose12 NEAR boot descends in front, FAR boot rear/toe, transitioning into pose1.
Most crucial: NEAR leg must genuinely move from FORWARD to CENTER to BACK during first half, then swing from BACK to CENTER to FORWARD during second half. Do not keep near leg pointing forward in all cells. Image2 exact red and blue boot/knee positions specify this. Don't draw both feet planted in passing poses. Show trouser knees and lower legs clearly; parted coat shouldn't hide all gait mechanics. Preserve knee-length coat length, coat sides shift subtly with the legs, no giant windblown triangular cape. Torso remains stable with slight weight transfer; head never rotates. Natural believable weighted heel-to-toe steps, no running or exaggerated high-knee march. Make each drawing clean and crisp with consistent costume and anatomy.
